name: The West Indian Day Parade at Full Volume
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: Eastern Parkway at the peak with the sound systems and the feathers and the whole diaspora at once, and a woman in full mas costume has stopped dead centre and raised both arms and the entire parkway has answered

name: The Protest That Filled the Bridge
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the Brooklyn Bridge walkway solid with people from tower to tower, entirely silent by agreement, and a young organiser in the middle has just realised how far back it goes

name: The Marathon at Mile Eighteen
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: First Avenue with the crowd four deep and a runner who is done, entirely done, being carried forward by nothing but the noise, and a stranger has just put a hand out

name: The Blackout Block Party
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bushwick street the second night of an outage where somebody has run a generator to a sound system and the whole neighbourhood is out, and the grill is going and nobody is afraid

name: The Lunar New Year on Mott Street
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the lion dance coming down a packed street in red smoke with the drums going, and a child on a father's shoulders has just been reached for by the lion

name: The Pride March That Went Past Midnight
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: Fifth Avenue still full at one in the morning because nobody would leave, and an older marcher who was at the first one is being carried on a float by people who were not born

name: The Vigil on the Corner
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bronx intersection full of candles and eight hundred quiet people, and the mother at the centre is being held up by four women who were strangers a week ago

name: The Puerto Rican Day Crowd on Fifth
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the flags going the whole length of the avenue and the sound of it, and a grandmother in the crowd has just seen her granddaughter go past in the parade

name: The Gathering
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: an enormous impossible crowd filling a great public square in New York at dusk, every kind of gathering this city does happening at once and somehow coherently, a parade coming through one side and a protest on another and a block party and a vigil and a marathon finish and a wedding and a street fair, hundreds of thousands of faces of every origin and age, and rising from the centre of it a vast column of light made of the shared feeling of the crowd, and one small figure at the base of it is looking directly out at the viewer, eye flowers opening in a full ring around the entire square

name: The Yankee Stadium Crowd on Its Feet
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: fifty thousand people up at once in the bottom of the ninth and the sound arriving physically, and a father and a daughter who have not agreed on anything in a year are holding on to each other

name: The Street Fair on Ninth Avenue
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: forty blocks of it in September with the smoke and the crowd and the same twelve stalls repeating, and a couple who met at this fair eleven years ago are back

name: The Funeral That Closed the Avenue
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Harlem procession with a brass band and two thousand people walking behind, and the widow at the front is walking absolutely upright

name: The Crowd at the Ferry Terminal at Six
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the doors open and four thousand people move as one organism through the hall, and a tourist standing still in the middle of it is having the best moment of her trip

name: The Rally in Foley Square
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the square full in the rain and nobody leaving, and a speaker with no amplification is being repeated outward by the crowd in rings

name: The New Year on a Rooftop
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Queens roof at midnight with forty people who all live in the building and the whole skyline going off around them, and two of them have just decided something

name: The Line Outside the Sneaker Shop
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Soho block where three hundred people have slept out and have become, over sixteen hours, a genuine community that will dissolve at ten in the morning, and somebody has brought coffee for everyone

name: The Second Line Through Bed Stuy
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a brass band leading a growing crowd down Marcy on a Sunday afternoon and the number of people is doubling every block, and the trumpet player at the front is not looking back

name: The Crowd That Stopped for the Fire
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: an entire Queens block outside at two in the morning watching a building go, and the moment the last family comes out the whole crowd makes a sound together

name: The Halloween Parade in the Village
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: Sixth Avenue in full costume chaos where the puppets are eleven feet tall and the crowd is indistinguishable from the parade, and a small child in a homemade costume is being cheered by two hundred strangers

name: The Waiting Room at Ellis Island
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the great hall full again for one afternoon with the descendants of everyone who came through it, and a woman standing on the exact tile where her great grandmother stood is looking up at the same ceiling

name: The Crowd Under the Tree at Rockefeller
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the whole world pressed into one plaza in December and every single person happy in the same simple way, and a man who has hated this his whole life is enjoying it enormously

name: The Anti Eviction Blockade
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bushwick doorway with two hundred neighbours in front of it arm in arm, entirely calm, and the family in the window above is watching the block hold

name: The Cricket Match in Van Cortlandt
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: eleven simultaneous matches on a Bronx field on a Sunday with four hundred spectators from six countries, and a boy has just taken a catch that the entire park has seen

name: The Concert in the Park
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the Great Lawn with a hundred thousand people lying down at once in the dark listening, and one woman sitting up has looked around and understood what she is in the middle of

name: The Last Train Car at Two AM
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a crowded late car full of every kind of New Yorker going home, entirely peaceful, and a drunk kid asleep on a stranger's shoulder is being let sleep by everyone in the car

name: The Arrivals Hall at Four in the Morning
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a JFK terminal where a family that has waited eleven years is watching a door, and it opens, and the woman coming through it is carrying one bag

name: The First Apartment
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a young woman standing alone in an empty Ridgewood room with the keys in her hand and the whole thing entirely hers, and the light is coming in

name: The Man at the Naturalisation Ceremony
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a hall in Lower Manhattan and a man in a good suit at the moment it becomes true, and his daughter in the audience is filming it badly and crying

name: The Last Box Out of the Old Place
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bay Ridge stoop and a man carrying the final box out of an apartment he lived in for twenty six years, and he has stopped on the step and is looking back up at the window

name: The Woman Who Arrived Yesterday
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Roosevelt Avenue sidewalk and a woman who landed thirty hours ago standing in the noise and the smell and the light of it, and something in her face has just decided that this is going to work

name: The Hospital Door at Both Ends
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bronx hospital entrance where a family is coming out with a newborn and another family is going in for the last time, passing in the doorway, and both know exactly what the other is

name: The Border of Two Neighbourhoods
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a single Brooklyn street where one side is one world and the other side is another, and a teenager who belongs to both is standing in the middle of the road, entirely comfortable

name: The Man Who Came Back After Twenty Years Inside
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Queens sidewalk and a man in his fifties standing outside a building he last saw in 2006, and his sister is coming down the steps

name: The Wedding on the Courthouse Steps
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: two people just married by the city coming out into the sun with eleven relatives and one bouquet from a corner deli, and a stranger passing has stopped to clap

name: The Bus Station at Christmas
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: Port Authority full of people going somewhere that matters, and a young man with a duffel who has not been home in four years is at gate level looking at the departure

name: The Threshold of the Mosque at Eid
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bay Ridge doorway with shoes filling the whole entrance and light coming out, and a convert attending her first Eid is standing at the edge of it being welcomed in

name: The Woman Who Is Leaving New York
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Greenpoint rooftop at dawn with a packed car on the street below and a woman taking one last look, and she is going to come back and she does not know that yet

name: The Fire Door That Was Always Locked
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Harlem school's back door opens for the first time in thirty years onto a courtyard nobody knew was there, full of grown trees, and the custodian who turned the key is standing in it

name: The Man Who Sleeps in the Doorway
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Midtown entrance at five in the morning where the doorman has left a coffee on the step as he does every day, and the man in the doorway has just woken to find it

name: The Customs Line
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a hall of people from everywhere waiting with total patience, and an officer at a booth has just done something small and human that the whole line has noticed

name: The Stoop Where the Whole Family Waits
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Crown Heights stoop with four generations on it at seven in the evening waiting for one car to turn the corner, and it has just turned the corner

name: The Woman Who Opens the Shop Every Morning
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Sunset Park shutter going up at six for the eleven thousandth time and the street coming into the shop with the light, and she is exactly where she wants to be

name: The Elevator Doors at the Job Interview
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a young woman in a borrowed jacket in a Financial District lobby at the moment the doors open, and she has decided to walk in like she owns it

name: The Doorway of the Place That Is Closing
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Village storefront on its final evening with forty regulars in it and the owner in the doorway looking in at all of them at once

name: The Airport Curb at Departures
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a woman putting her mother into a taxi after three weeks and neither of them is doing the thing where you pretend it is fine

name: The Gate of the Cemetery on a Visiting Day
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Queens cemetery entrance with families coming through in both directions carrying flowers, and a man arriving alone with nothing has stopped at the gate

name: The Threshold of the Recovery Meeting
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a church basement doorway and a man who has been standing outside it for twenty minutes, and someone inside has just come to the door and said something ordinary

name: The Front Door of the House the Family Finally Bought
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Cambria Heights porch with a whole family on it and a key going into a lock for the first time, and the grandmother whose forty years of work paid for this is the one holding it

name: The Turnstile on the First Day of the Job
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a man in a new uniform going through a subway gate at five in the morning toward the first shift of a job he was told he would never get

name: The Door That Is Always Open
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Bronx apartment where the door has genuinely not been locked since 1991 and the whole floor comes and goes, and the woman inside is asleep in a chair with three neighbours quietly in her kitchen

name: The Street That Is Only There on Tuesdays
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a block in the West Village that exists one day a week and the people who live on it accept the arrangement completely, and a woman who found it by accident on a Tuesday has come back on a Wednesday and is standing where it should be

name: The Reflection That Arrives Late
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: every window on one Financial District block shows what happened four seconds ago, and a man who has just dropped something is watching himself still holding it

name: The Woman Who Is In Two Places
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Queens woman is genuinely at work and at her mother's bedside simultaneously and neither version knows about the other, and one of them has just noticed something

name: The Building With One More Floor Than It Has
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Murray Hill tower where the count from inside and the count from the street differ by one, and the surveyor who has done it eleven times is standing on the sidewalk looking up

name: The Man Who Is Always Just Ahead
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a figure who is on every block a woman turns onto, at the far end, walking away, for eleven years, and today he has stopped and is waiting for her

name: The Room at the End of the Hall
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Harlem apartment whose hallway is longer at night and ends in a door the residents have agreed not to discuss, and the child of the family is standing in front of it with a hand up

name: The Card Trick on the Corner
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Times Square street magician performs something for one tourist that is genuinely impossible and both of them know it, and the magician looks as surprised as she does

name: The Twin Nobody Else Can See
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Staten Island man has been accompanied by an identical figure his whole life, always slightly behind, and the photograph his wife has just taken has two of him in it

name: The Mirror at the Centre of the City
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: in an ordinary Midtown lobby stands a mirror that shows the viewer the city rather than themselves, the entire five boroughs alive and moving in the glass at once, every street and every person, and an ordinary office worker who stopped to fix her collar is now standing in front of it unable to move, the whole reflected city blooming with eye flowers and a single small figure at the centre of the reflection looking directly back out at her, the real lobby behind her utterly plain and beige and unremarkable

name: The Sound That Comes From No Direction
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a note audible on one Inwood block since 1997 that has no source and no direction, and a physicist who came to solve it has been sitting in a lawn chair for six hours entirely happy

name: The Photograph Everyone Remembers Differently
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: an image in a Brooklyn family's hallway that every member of the family describes differently and all of them are correct, and three of them are standing in front of it disagreeing warmly

name: The Subway Car With Nobody On It
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a fully lit empty car runs through the system every night and stops properly at every station, doors opening, and a woman on a platform at three has decided to get on

name: The Cat That Is In Every Photograph
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a tabby appears in the background of every picture ever taken on one Bushwick block since 2011 regardless of when, and a photographer reviewing forty rolls has found it again

name: The Apartment That Is Bigger Inside
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Lower East Side studio that has eleven rooms once the door closes, and the tenant paying studio rent is having six friends to dinner in a dining room that cannot exist

name: The Man Who Remembers Tomorrow
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Queens barber who has always remembered the next day rather than the last and has therefore never been surprised, and he has just gone very quiet mid cut

name: The Shadow That Belongs to the Building
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Tribeca facade casts the shadow of a different building entirely, one that stood there before, and an architectural historian has laid out a plan and matched it exactly

name: The Woman Who Has Been Here Before
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a tourist from Ohio in Washington Square who knows the location of a bench that was moved in 1962 and has never been to New York, and she has just walked directly to where it was

name: The Door in the Retaining Wall
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a small iron door in a Riverside Park wall that opens onto a lit corridor going west under the river, and a jogger who has run past it for six years has stopped and tried it and it opened

name: The Snow That Fell Only on One Building
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: an inch on a single Bronx tenement and nowhere else in the borough, and the residents are on the roof making a snowman in seventy degree weather

name: The Number That Everyone Sees
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: an unexplained shape appears in the corner of every reflective surface in the city for one week, identical everywhere, and the whole of New York has quietly agreed to pretend not to notice, and a woman on a bus is the first to point at it out loud

name: The Bodega That Sells the Thing You Lost
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a Brooklyn corner store with one shelf behind the counter holding whatever the customer most recently lost, and a man is being handed a set of keys he lost in 2004

name: The Block That Dreams Together
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: one Sunset Park street where everybody has the same dream on the same night four times a year and nobody has ever discussed it, and this morning two neighbours on the stoop have accidentally started to

name: The Person Who Is Not In the Photograph
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: a group picture on a Bronx fridge in which every family member is certain somebody is missing and no two of them name the same person, and the youngest has just said a name that has silenced the kitchen

name: The Second City Above the First
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the entire island of Manhattan asleep and dreaming, and the dream is visible above it as a second city built of light standing on the real one, the buildings that were never built and the ones that were torn down and the ones that only exist in what people remember, the elevated lines back and the old Penn Station whole and a hundred impossible towers, and one insomniac on a Brooklyn roof across the river is the only person awake enough to see it, eye flowers opening in cascade through both cities at once

name: The Answer
era: XV THE CITY THAT ANSWERS BACK
brief: the very last frame, an ordinary New Yorker standing on an ordinary corner in the early morning light, entirely alone, entirely calm, looking directly at the viewer, and behind her the whole of Era XV is arranged in one enormous receding perspective, the grid and the weather and the night shift and the sixth borough and the faiths and the food and the market and the repair and the archive and the bodies and the sound and the transit and the runway and the machines and the green and the kids and the elders and the crowd and the thresholds and the dreams, every character of this era present and small and going about their lives in one continuous impossible city, and she is the one who was asked the question and she is about to answer it, one hand slightly raised, eye flowers opening from every surface all the way to the horizon and one glowing evil eye on her wrist
